title: The localized signed Hom action of a two-term perfect coefficient object
statement: Let Y be a scheme and R a commutative ring sheaf on its pro-etale site, with coefficient universe max(u,t+1). Use the module, tensor, Hom-complex, derived Hom and canonical homModelMap of [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models]. Let P,I,Q,Q0 be complexes of R-module sheaves. Assume P,Q,Q0 are K-flat and I is K-injective. Suppose Q0 is zero outside degrees -1,0, both remaining terms are isomorphic to the R-module unit, and there is an isomorphism Qloc(Q) to Qloc(Q0) in the derived category. If f:Hom(P,I) tensor Q to Hom(P,I tensor Q) satisfies the signed local evaluation formula of [lem-sf-two-term-free-hom-tensor-components], then Qloc(f) followed by homModelMap(P,I tensor Q) is invertible. This asserts neither invertibility of f itself nor K-injectivity of I tensor Q, and has no scalar reduction presentation as input.

proof.text: For Q0, the component theorem makes the signed exchange invertible as a chain map. The bounded coefficient complex of unit terms is dualizable, with bounded K-flat dual. Tensoring with Q0 preserves K-injectives by the tensor-dual adjunction on the homotopy category. Thus homModelMap(P,I tensor Q0) is an isomorphism: the canonical target augmentation is a homotopy equivalence between K-injectives and Hom preserves it.

source.place: paragraphs 1-2: two-term perfect coefficient object and scalar extension-restriction adjunction

proof.text: Represent the given isomorphism Qloc(Q) to Qloc(Q0) by a roof with K-flat complexes. A quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes has acyclic K-flat cone, and hence remains a quasi-isomorphism after tensoring with any complex. Apply this to Hom(P,I) and I. Derived Hom carries the resulting target isomorphism to an isomorphism.

source.place: paragraphs 1-2: two-term perfect coefficient object and scalar extension-restriction adjunction

proof.text: The signed exchange is natural in the coefficient complex. Its formula determines it by the Hom product projections and tensor-sheafification descent; for each map of the roof both composites have that same formula. Naturality of homModelMap descends the commutative square to the derived category. All its vertical arrows are isomorphisms, so invertibility for Q0 proves invertibility for Q.

theorem perfectCoefficient_signedHomAction_isIso
    (P I Q Q0 : CochainComplex (Modules.{t, u} Y R) ℤ)
    (hP : flat.{t, u} Y R P) (hI : I.IsKInjective)
    (hQ : flat.{t, u} Y R Q) (hQ0 : flat.{t, u} Y R Q0)
    (hzero : ∀ k : ℤ, k ≠ -1 → k ≠ 0 → IsZero (Q0.X k))
    (eNeg : Q0.X (-1) ≅ (show Modules.{t, u} Y R from SheafOfModules.unit
      ((sheafCompose (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology Y)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)} RingCat.{max u (t + 1)})).obj R)))
    (eZero : Q0.X 0 ≅ (show Modules.{t, u} Y R from SheafOfModules.unit
      ((sheafCompose (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology Y)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)} RingCat.{max u (t + 1)})).obj R)))
    (eQ : DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q0)
    (f : ((totalTensor.{t, u} Y R).obj
        (homComplex.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), max u (t + 1)} (R := R) P I)).obj Q ⟶
      homComplex.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), max u (t + 1)} (R := R) P
        (((totalTensor.{t, u} Y R).obj I).obj Q))
    (hf : IsSignedHomTensor Y R P I Q f) :
    IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map f ≫
      homModelMap.{t, u} Y R P (((totalTensor.{t, u} Y R).obj I).obj Q))
